text:
Mia R.: heads-up, tenant-834 reports widespread 502s from hosted inference starting ~08:12 UTC. Example req id: req_0a9f3c. Customer says failures are intermittent but high volume. Can SRE/eng take a look?
Samir: looking now — any sample curl/log from customer?
Mia R.: pasted what they sent: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\nDate: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 08:12:43 GMT\nContent-Type: application/json\n{"error":"gateway error","request_id":"req_0a9f3c"}
```
Customers seeing consistent 502s, latency spikes before failing.
Samir: pulling control-plane logs for auth/session/routing-policy and config-db. Quick look: auth-service is throwing repeated "configdb timeout" errors at 08:11:58 and then returning 500s which propagate as 502s at the gateway. snippet from auth-service: 
```
ERROR auth-service request_id=req_0a9f3c user=tenant-834 session=abc123 error="configdb_read_timeout: deadline exceeded" backend=cfg-db-01
WARN session-manager failed to validate session: backend timeout
```
Nora Ops: metrics show a config DB 95th latency jump at 08:10:50, concurrent connections spike ~3x. routing-policy-service also started returning 500s shortly after. rolling window correlates with a deployment to configdb read replica group? CPU and IO on cfg-db-host-3 at 08:09.
James L.: I can scale up routing-policy pods and restart the failing replica of config-db read pool. Propose temporary mitigation: flip gateway fallback to model-variant-less-auth (less strict routing) so hosted API can bypass policy check for tenant-834 while we stabilize. That will be a temporary risk tradeoff (routing checks relaxed).
David - eng-sre: +1 on rolling restart. Also recommend increasing configdb client timeout from 1.2s -> 2.5s as emergency mitigation so transient spikes don't return 5xx immediately. I have the kubectl commands: 
```
# restart routing-policy deployment
kubectl -n controlplane rollout restart deploy/routing-policy --context=cluster-hosted
# cordon and drain cfg-db-host-3 then restart db process
ssh admin@cfg-db-host-3 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-configdb'
```
Samir: started the rollout restart of routing-policy (deploy/routing-policy) at 08:14:20 UTC. Observability: routing-policy 5xx count dropping after restart, but configdb latency still high.
support-bot: Incident created INC-2026-1347 by Samir. Pager notified.
Mia R.: updated customer: "We're investigating; temporary mitigation in progress, will update in 15m." they asked for repro steps and whether this is tenant-specific.
Nora Ops: preliminary: not tenant-specific; configdb read pool saturation affected several tenants but tenant-834 triggered worst path because they hit heavy auth+session validations. Graph: configdb connections peaked then dropped after host reboot at 08:19.
James L.: after routing-policy restart and host reboot, gateway 502s dropped to baseline by 08:21. We should keep monitors on for 30m and then rollback TTL change if it was part of recent commit.
David - eng-sre: found related commit in infra repo that reduced configdb client-side connection pool size (commit 0a1b2c) deployed 07:58 — that lowered effective concurrency and amplified spike. I'll open a rollback PR.
Samir: actions tracked: 1) scale routing-policy to +2 replicas (done) 2) restart cfg-db-host-3 (done) 3) increase configdb client timeout temporarily (in progress) 4) rollback commit 0a1b2c (WIP) 5) customer comms (Mia).
Mia R.: customer updated and appreciated fast response. They asked for postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.
James L.: plan for permanent fix: revert pool-size change, add better client backpressure, and add an autoscale alarm on configdb RPS/conn. Will prepare rollout plan and runbook updates.
David - eng-sre: leaving follow-up tasks in INC-2026-1347: root cause = configdb client pool reduction + transient IO spike on cfg-db-host-3 causing auth/session validation failures -> gateway 502 propagation. Next steps: revert, increase read pool capacity, improve circuit-breaker behavior in auth-service.
Mia R.: thanks team. Please add timeline and ownership to the incident. I'll notify account team and send a short RCA to tenant-834 after postmortem. :thumbsup:
Samir: tagging @eng-oncall for follow-up actions.
